sentences.text: This appeal coming on for Hearing, through physical hearing/video conference, this day T.G.Shivashankare Gowda, J., delivered the following:
JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the appellants have challenged the judgment dated 30.01.2017 passed in M.V.C.No.792/2015 on the file of MACT, Vijayapura (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).
2. The appellants were the petitioners and respondents were the respondents before the Tribunal.
The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Briefly stated, the facts are that, the 1st petitioner is the daughter-in-law and the 2nd to 4th petitioners are the grand children of Thangewwa, the deceased.
The deceased suffered severe injuries and succumbed to death in a road accident that took place on 12-03-2015 near Soundatti when a Cruiser Jeep bearing registration No.KA-28/M-3976 ran over her.
Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
They pleaded that deceased was aged 55 years, doing agriculture and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.1,73,000/- with 9% interest.

4. The petitioners have pleaded inadequacy in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the ground that the income of the deceased as an agricultural worker was not considered by the Tribunal and compensation was not properly assessed under conventional heads.

5. According to the learned counsel for petitioners, the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month, multiplier applicable is '11' and compensation towards conventional heads has to be considered as per settled principles and accordingly he sought for re-assessment and enhancement.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company contended that the petitioners are not the dependents of the deceased, they are majors rather the deceased was dependent on them, utmost loss of estate may be assessed to a small extent and sought to modify the impugned judgment.

Learned counsel placed reliance on the judgment of a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of A.Manavalagan Vs. A.Krishnamurthy and Others (ILR 2004 KAR 3268).

sentences.text: We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of the deceased due to injuries and the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
The evidence on record do point out that the deceased was a widow of 56 years old; PW1 admits that they were taking care of the deceased soon before her death.
Hence, we are of the opinion that the petitioners were not dependents on the deceased.

This court in the above referred judgment held that where the claim by the legal representatives of the deceased who were not dependents of the deceased, then the basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, which is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It is further discussed that the procedure for determination of loss to estate is broadly the same as the procedure for determination of the loss of dependency.
It was also held that the claimants being non-dependents, the savings can be assessed at 15% of the income of the deceased.
9. The deceased was an agricultural worker; the accident was of the year 2015; notional income of the deceased has to be considered at Rs.8,000/- for a person who has no proof of income.

The Tribunal considered the income at Rs.1,500/- per month, deducted 1/3rd of it and considered Rs.12,000/- as annual income and multiplied by '9' arrived at Rs.1,08,000/- and added loss of love and affection at Rs.40,000/-, towards transportation and funeral Rs.25,000/- in arriving at Rs.1,73,000/-.

10. In view of our findings, the petitioners being not dependents, the calculation will be the same procedure for calculation of loss of income by adding future prospects of 10% for the age of the deceased as '56' by applying the principles laid down in National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others -2017 ACJ 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Applicable multiplier for the age of 56 as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. DTC- (2009)6 SCC 121, is '9' and it is correctly applied by the Tribunal.
11.

If all these factors are taken into consideration, the assessment of loss of income would be:
Rs.8,000/- plus future prospects of 10% (Rs.800/-) = Rs.8,800/- minus 1/3rd (Rs.2,933/-) =
Rs.5867/- per month and multiplied by multiplier '9' for the age of 56 comes to Rs.6,33,636/-, 15%
of it comes to Rs.95,045/- and it will be the loss of estate the petitioners are entitled to.
As seen from the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- only towards loss of love and affection, and funeral expenses and loss of estate of Rs.25,000/-, which is not proper.
The deceased left her 3 grandchildren and caring daughter-in-law.

Towards loss of love and affection, Rs.40,000/-
each has to be assessed apart from Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
Then the total compensation comes to Rs.2,70,045/- as against Rs.1,73,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.97,045/- rounded off to Rs.97,000/-.
Accordingly, the appeal deserves to the allowed.

12. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.
